newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.30 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.30 cent higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.30 cent per lb firmer on Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, dealers said.

They said the supply and demand data released this morning should lend support to an otherwise weak market. The U.S. Commerce Department put consumption at an annualized 10.96 million 480-lb bales in April, compared with an adjusted rate of 10.58 million bales in March.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged new sales of upland cotton for the week ended May 15 at 112,100 in the old crop and at 86,400 bales in the new crop.
"These numbers should staunch the blood flow," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, pegging resistance at 72.50 cents, followed by 73.00 cents basis July.
Traders noted buy stops 74.10 cents in July.
Wednesday, the spot month closed down 0.23 cents at 72.12 cents, having ranged from 72.55 to 72.10 cents. New-crop December ended 0.25 cent weaker at 74.52 cents.
Activity is expected to remain thin ahead of the long Memorial Day weekend, when the American Cotton Shippers' Association will also hold its annual meeting, in West Virginia.
